vi.L: Vào ngày của Chúa, tôi ở trong Thánh Linh, và tôi nghe phía sau tôi có một tiếng lớn như [tiếng] kèn, \v 11 nói: "Điều con thấy, hãy chép vào một cuộn sách và gửi cho bảy Hội Thánh: cho Ê-phê-sô, cho Si-miệc-nơ, cho Bẹt-găm, cho Thi-a-ti-rơ, cho Sạt-đe, cho Phi-la-đen-phi và cho Lao-đi-xê."
vi.B: Vào ngày của Chúa, tôi được ở trong Thánh Linh, và tôi nghe phía sau mình có một tiếng lớn vang lên như tiếng kèn. \v 11 Tiếng ấy nói: "Hãy chép vào một cuộn sách những gì con đang thấy, rồi gửi cho bảy Hội Thánh: Ê-phê-sô, Si-miệc-nơ, Bẹt-găm, Thi-a-ti-rơ, Sạt-đe, Phi-la-đen-phi và Lao-đi-xê."
vi.R: Đó là ngày của Chúa, và Thánh Linh đã cầm giữ lấy tôi. Tôi nghe một tiếng lớn ở phía sau tôi. Tiếng ấy vang lên như tiếng kèn. \v 11 Tiếng ấy nói: "Hãy chép vào một cuộn sách những gì con thấy. Rồi gửi cuộn sách ấy cho bảy Hội Thánh ở các thành này: Ê-phê-sô, Si-miệc-nơ, Bẹt-găm, Thi-a-ti-rơ, Sạt-đe, Phi-la-đen-phi và Lao-đi-xê."

ko.L: 나는 주님의 날에 성령 안에 있었다. 그리고 내 뒤에서 나팔 소리 같은 큰 음성을 들었다. \v 11 [그 음성이] 말씀하셨다. "네가 보는 것을 두루마리에 기록하여 일곱 교회, 곧 에베소와 서머나와 버가모와 두아디라와 사데와 빌라델비아와 라오디게아로 보내라."
ko.B: 주님의 날에 나는 성령에 사로잡혔다. 그때 내 뒤에서 나팔 소리 같은 큰 음성이 들렸다. \v 11 그 음성이 말씀하셨다. "네가 보는 것을 두루마리에 기록하여 일곱 교회, 곧 에베소, 서머나, 버가모, 두아디라, 사데, 빌라델비아, 라오디게아에 보내라."
ko.R: 그날은 주님의 날이었다. 성령께서 나를 사로잡으셨다. 나는 내 뒤에서 큰 음성을 들었다. 그 음성은 나팔 소리 같았다. \v 11 그 음성이 말씀하셨다. "네가 보는 것을 두루마리에 적어라. 그리고 그것을 이 도시들에 있는 일곱 교회에 보내라. 에베소, 서머나, 버가모, 두아디라, 사데, 빌라델비아, 라오디게아이다."

pt.L: Estive no Espírito no dia do Senhor, e ouvi atrás de mim uma voz forte como [a] de uma trombeta, \v 11 dizendo: "O que você vê, escreva num rolo e envie às sete igrejas: a Éfeso, e a Esmirna, e a Pérgamo, e a Tiatira, e a Sardes, e a Filadélfia, e a Laodiceia."
pt.B: No dia do Senhor, eu estava no Espírito e ouvi atrás de mim uma voz forte, que soava como uma trombeta. \v 11 Ela disse: "Escreva num rolo o que você está vendo e envie-o às sete igrejas: a Éfeso, Esmirna, Pérgamo, Tiatira, Sardes, Filadélfia e Laodiceia."
pt.R: Era o dia do Senhor, e o Espírito tomou conta de mim. Ouvi atrás de mim uma voz forte. Ela soava como uma trombeta. \v 11 A voz disse: "Escreva num rolo o que você está vendo. Depois mande o rolo às sete igrejas destas cidades: Éfeso, Esmirna, Pérgamo, Tiatira, Sardes, Filadélfia e Laodiceia."

decisions.choice: in the Spirit: under the power of God's Spirit, able to see visions
alternatives: in a trance, a state of the human spirit
decisions.reason: πνεύματι has no article and could describe John's own state, "in spirit". But in Revelation the visions come by the Spirit of God (4:2; 17:3; 21:10), as they did for Ezekiel (Ezekiel 3:12-14; 11:1), so it is taken here as the Holy Spirit.

decisions.choice: the Lord's day: the first day of the week, when Christians met
alternatives: the day of the Lord, the day of judgment, into which John is carried in vision
decisions.reason: κυριακῇ is an adjective, "belonging to the Lord", the same word Paul uses of the Lord's supper (1 Corinthians 11:20). Christian writers from soon after use "the Lord's day" for Sunday, the day of the resurrection, when believers gathered (compare Acts 20:7). The Old Testament "day of the Lord" is a different phrase.

decisions.choice: a scroll: a written roll, the usual form of a book
decisions.reason: βιβλίον means a written document. In John's day books were written on rolls of papyrus or parchment; bound books were just coming into use. Revelation later speaks of scrolls that are rolled up and sealed (5:1; 6:14).

decisions.choice: seven cities on a road through the province of Asia
decisions.reason: The seven cities lie in the order a messenger would reach them on a circuit, starting at Ephesus on the coast and going north, then east and south. Chapters 2-3 hold the message to each church in the same order.

decisions.choice: scroll (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: "Book" makes an English reader picture a bound volume. "Scroll" names the object John would have used (m3).

decisions.choice: the Spirit took hold of me (R)
decisions.reason: "In the Spirit" is not plain English for a young reader. Readable says what it means: John was under the Spirit's power. It depends on the uncertain decision m1.

decisions.choice: "un rouleau" (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: As in English, "un livre" makes a reader picture a bound volume; "un rouleau" names the object John would have written on (m3). The same word is used for the scroll with seven seals in chapter 5.

decisions.choice: rollo
decisions.reason: A "libro" today is a bound book with pages; the Greek word here is a written roll, the usual form of a book then. "Rollo" keeps that picture, which matters again in chapter 5.

decisions.choice: Éfeso, Esmirna, Pérgamo, Tiatira, Sardis, Filadelfia, Laodicea
decisions.reason: The usual Spanish forms of the seven city names. "Sardis" is the form most Spanish readers know; "Sardes" is also used.

decisions.choice: Efeso, Smirna, Pergamo, Thiatira, Sardi, Filadelfia, Laodikia
decisions.reason: The usual Swahili forms of the seven city names; Efeso (Ephesians 1:1), Thiatira (Acts 16:14) and Laodikia (Colossians 2:1) as already used in the Swahili New Testament. The same through chapters 2 and 3.

decisions.choice: gombo
decisions.reason: "Gombo" is a written roll, the Swahili word for scroll used in Luke 4:17; "kitabu" would suggest a bound book (m3).

decisions.choice: "Ê-phê-sô, Si-miệc-nơ, Bẹt-găm, Thi-a-ti-rơ, Sạt-đe, Phi-la-đen-phi, Lao-đi-xê"; "con" for John in the heavenly voice's words; "cuộn sách"
decisions.reason: The Protestant forms of the seven cities, "Lao-đi-xê" as in the Vietnamese Colossians (4:13). The voice that speaks to John is the risen Christ's (1:12-18), who speaks to his servant as "con", as Jesus speaks to his disciples in the Vietnamese Gospels.

decisions.choice: "성령 안에" (L), "성령에 사로잡혀" (B, R); "두루마리" for the scroll; the seven cities in their Protestant forms (에베소, 서머나, 버가모, 두아디라, 사데, 빌라델비아, 라오디게아)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads "in the Spirit" as under the power of God's Spirit (uncertain, footnoted). The voice is Christ's (1:12-13), so the narrative gives it the honorific ("말씀하셨다").

decisions.choice: um rolo
decisions.reason: For the whole book, for every scroll John sees (5:1-9; 10:2-10). "Livro" makes a reader picture a bound volume, as English "book" does (m3); "pergaminho" names a material, and these scrolls could be papyrus. The fixed phrase "o livro da vida" (3:5) keeps "livro", as Portuguese readers know it.

decisions.choice: a trombeta
decisions.reason: For the whole book, here and for the seven trumpets of chapters 8-11: "trombeta" is the ordinary Portuguese word and the one Brazilian readers know for this book.

decisions.choice: você
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the risen Christ and his angels speak to John with "você", as Jesus speaks to one person in the Gospels (style section 4); "tu" is kept for words addressed to God and the Lamb (chapters 4-5).

source.text: Καὶ ἐπέστρεψα βλέπειν τὴν φωνὴν ἥτις ἐλάλει μετ’ ἐμοῦ· καὶ ἐπιστρέψας εἶδον ἑπτὰ λυχνίας χρυσᾶς, καὶ ἐν μέσῳ τῶν λυχνιῶν ὅμοιον υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου, ἐνδεδυμένον ποδήρη καὶ περιεζωσμένον πρὸς τοῖς μαστοῖς ζώνην χρυσᾶν·

en.L: And I turned to see the voice that was speaking with me, and having turned I saw seven golden lampstands, \v 13 and in [the] middle of the lampstands [one] like a son of man, clothed [in a robe reaching] to the feet and wrapped around at the chest [with] a golden sash.
en.B: I turned around to see whose voice it was that spoke with me, and as I turned I saw seven lampstands made of gold. \v 13 In the middle of the lampstands was one like a son of man. A long robe came down to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, and a gold sash was tied around {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chest.
en.R: I turned around to see who was speaking to me. When I turned, I saw seven lampstands made of gold. \v 13 Someone was standing among the lampstands. He looked like a son of man, a human being. He was wearing a long robe that came down to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet. A gold sash was tied across {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chest.

fr.L: Et je me retournai pour voir la voix qui parlait avec moi ; et m’étant retourné, je vis sept chandeliers d’or, \v 13 et au milieu des chandeliers [quelqu’un] semblable à un fils d’homme, vêtu [d’une robe descendant] jusqu’aux pieds et ceint à la poitrine d’une ceinture d’or.
fr.B: Je me retournai pour voir de qui venait la voix qui me parlait, et en me retournant je vis sept chandeliers d’or. \v 13 Au milieu des chandeliers se tenait quelqu’un qui ressemblait à un fils d’homme. Il portait une longue robe qui descendait jusqu’à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds, et une ceinture d’or était nouée autour de {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} poitrine.
fr.R: Je me suis retourné pour voir qui me parlait. En me retournant, j’ai vu sept chandeliers en or. \v 13 Quelqu’un se tenait au milieu des chandeliers. Il ressemblait à un fils d’homme, c’est-à-dire à un être humain. Il portait une longue robe qui descendait jusqu’à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds. Une ceinture en or était attachée sur {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} poitrine.

es.L: Y me volví para ver la voz que hablaba conmigo; y habiéndome vuelto, vi siete candelabros de oro, \v 13 y en medio de los candelabros [a uno] semejante a un hijo de hombre, vestido [con una túnica que llegaba] hasta los pies y ceñido a la altura del pecho [con] un cinto de oro.
es.B: Me di la vuelta para ver de quién era la voz que hablaba conmigo, y al volverme vi siete candelabros de oro. \v 13 En medio de los candelabros estaba uno semejante a un hijo de hombre. Llevaba una túnica larga que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} llegaba hasta los pies, y un cinto de oro ceñido al pecho.
es.R: Me di la vuelta para ver quién me hablaba. Al volverme, vi siete candelabros de oro. \v 13 Entre los candelabros había alguien de pie. Parecía un hijo de hombre, un ser humano. Llevaba puesta una túnica larga que {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} llegaba hasta los pies. Tenía un cinto de oro atado sobre el pecho.

sw.L: Na nikageuka ili kuiona sauti iliyokuwa ikisema nami; na nilipogeuka niliona vinara saba vya taa vya dhahabu, \v 13 na katikati ya vinara [mmoja] aliye kama mwana wa mtu, amevaa [vazi refu hadi] miguuni, na amefungwa mshipi wa dhahabu kifuani.
sw.B: Niligeuka nione ni sauti ya nani iliyokuwa ikisema nami, na nilipogeuka niliona vinara saba vya taa vilivyotengenezwa kwa dhahabu. \v 13 Katikati ya vinara hivyo alikuwapo mmoja aliye kama mwana wa mtu. Alikuwa amevaa vazi refu lililofika miguuni {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}, na mshipi wa dhahabu ulikuwa umefungwa kifuani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}.
sw.R: Niligeuka nimwone aliyekuwa akisema nami. Nilipogeuka, niliona vinara saba vya taa vilivyotengenezwa kwa dhahabu. \v 13 Mtu fulani alikuwa amesimama katikati ya vinara hivyo. Alionekana kama mwana wa mtu, yaani mwanadamu. Alikuwa amevaa vazi refu lililofika miguuni {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}. Mshipi wa dhahabu ulikuwa umefungwa kifuani {{deity_pronoun:mwake|Mwake}}.

vi.L: Và tôi quay lại để xem tiếng đã nói với tôi; và khi quay lại, tôi thấy bảy chân đèn bằng vàng, \v 13 và ở giữa các chân đèn có [một Đấng] giống như con người, mặc [áo dài] đến chân, và ngực thắt một dây đai bằng vàng.
vi.B: Tôi quay lại để xem tiếng của ai đang nói với tôi, và khi quay lại, tôi thấy bảy chân đèn bằng vàng. \v 13 Ở giữa các chân đèn có một Đấng giống như con người. Ngài mặc một áo dài chấm chân, và ngực thắt một dây đai bằng vàng.
vi.R: Tôi quay lại để xem ai đang nói với tôi. Khi quay lại, tôi thấy bảy chân đèn bằng vàng. \v 13 Có một Đấng đứng giữa các chân đèn. Ngài trông giống như một con người. Ngài mặc một áo dài chấm đến chân. Một dây đai bằng vàng thắt ngang ngực {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그래서 나는 나에게 말씀하시는 음성을 보려고 돌아섰다. 돌아서자 나는 일곱 금 등잔대를 보았다. \v 13 그 등잔대들 한가운데 인자 같은 분이 계셨는데, 발까지 내려오는 옷을 입으시고 가슴에 금 띠를 띠고 계셨다.
ko.B: 나는 나에게 말씀하시는 음성이 누구의 것인지 보려고 돌아섰다. 돌아서자 금으로 만든 일곱 등잔대가 보였다. \v 13 그 등잔대들 한가운데 인자 같은 분이 계셨다. 그분은 발까지 내려오는 긴 옷을 입으시고, 가슴에는 금 띠를 매고 계셨다.
ko.R: 나는 누가 나에게 말씀하시는지 보려고 돌아섰다. 돌아서자 금으로 만든 일곱 등잔대가 보였다. \v 13 그 등잔대들 사이에 어떤 분이 서 계셨다. 그분은 사람의 아들 같은 분, 곧 사람의 모습을 하신 분이셨다. 그분은 발까지 내려오는 긴 옷을 입고 계셨다. 가슴에는 금 띠를 두르고 계셨다.

pt.L: E me voltei para ver a voz que falava comigo; e, tendo-me voltado, vi sete candelabros de ouro, \v 13 e no meio dos candelabros [alguém] semelhante a um filho de homem, vestido [com uma túnica que ia] até os pés e cingido no peito [com] uma faixa de ouro.
pt.B: Eu me virei para ver de quem era a voz que falava comigo e, ao me virar, vi sete candelabros de ouro. \v 13 No meio dos candelabros estava alguém semelhante a um filho de homem. Uma túnica longa descia até os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés, e uma faixa de ouro estava presa em volta do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} peito.
pt.R: Eu me virei para ver quem estava falando comigo. Quando me virei, vi sete candelabros de ouro. \v 13 Alguém estava de pé no meio dos candelabros. Ele parecia um filho de homem, um ser humano. Usava uma túnica longa que descia até os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés. Uma faixa de ouro estava amarrada em volta do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} peito.

decisions.choice: turned to see the voice: turned to see who was speaking
decisions.reason: To "see the voice" is a vivid way of saying that John turned to see the speaker.

decisions.choice: lampstands like the lampstand of the tabernacle and of Zechariah's vision
decisions.reason: A λυχνίας held oil lamps. The tabernacle had one gold lampstand with seven lamps (Exodus 25:31-40), and Zechariah saw one in a vision (Zechariah 4:2). Here there are seven, and 1:20 says they are the seven churches.

decisions.choice: one like a son of man: the figure of Daniel 7:13
alternatives: the title "the Son of Man" as Jesus used it in the Gospels
decisions.reason: ὅμοιον υἱὸν ἀνθρώπου, with no article, repeats Daniel 7:13, where "one like a son of man" means a figure in human form who receives God's kingdom. It is not quite the Gospels' title, "the Son of Man", which has the article, but it points to the same person: verses 17-18 show that he is Jesus.

decisions.choice: a long robe and a gold sash: dress of a priest, and of the heavenly figure in Daniel 10
decisions.reason: ποδήρη is a robe reaching to the feet. In the Greek Old Testament the same word is used for the high priest's robe (Exodus 28:4), and the man Daniel saw was clothed in linen with a belt of gold (Daniel 10:5). The dress suggests priestly and royal dignity; the text does not say more.

decisions.choice: whose voice it was (B); who was speaking (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "to see the voice"; Balanced and Readable say what the idiom means (m1).

decisions.choice: a son of man, lowercase (L, B, R); someone who looked human (R)
decisions.reason: Every level writes "a son of man" in lowercase, as Daniel 7:13 has it (m3), and Readable adds that the phrase means a human figure.

decisions.choice: lampstands
decisions.reason: These held oil lamps, not candles, so "lampstands" is the accurate word at every level.

decisions.choice: chest
decisions.reason: μαστοῖς here means the chest; the sash was worn high, not at the waist. "Chest" says this in plain English at every level.

decisions.choice: "chandeliers" (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: The English avoids anything that suggests candles. In French Bible language "chandelier" is the established word for the lampstand of the tabernacle and of Zechariah's vision (m2), which held oil lamps; "porte-lampes" is exact but rare and would hide that link. A native reviewer may prefer "porte-lampes".

decisions.choice: candelabros
decisions.reason: These are stands that hold lamps, like the lampstand of the tabernacle; "candelabro" is the word Hebrews 9:2 already uses for it. "Candelero" now usually means a holder for a single candle, and "lámpara" would name the light rather than the stand.

decisions.choice: semejante a un hijo de hombre (lowercase)
decisions.reason: John describes what he sees in the words of Daniel 7:13, without the article, so Spanish keeps it lowercase and indefinite, as the English does. "El Hijo del Hombre" is kept for Jesus's own title in the Gospels.

decisions.choice: mwana wa mtu, lowercase
decisions.reason: Here the phrase describes the figure of Daniel 7:13, one who looks human (m3), so Swahili says "mwana wa mtu" (a son of a human being) in lowercase, as the English keeps "a son of man" lowercase. The Gospels' title "Mwana wa Adamu" would make the vision name him instead of describing him. A reviewer may prefer the title, which links the passage with Jesus's own words.

decisions.choice: vinara vya taa
decisions.reason: "Kinara cha taa" is a lampstand, as in Hebrews 9:2; the plural "vinara vya taa" is used through the book.

decisions.choice: "[một Đấng] giống như con người" (L), "một Đấng giống như con người" (B, R), lowercase (also 14:14)
decisions.reason: The figure is the one of Daniel 7:13 (m3), and the English keeps "a son of man" in lowercase. Vietnamese "con người" in lowercase means a human being, and the same words with capitals are the title "Con Người" of the Gospels, so the echo is kept without making the phrase a title here. "Đấng" marks him as the risen Christ.

decisions.choice: "인자 같은 분" (L, B); "사람의 아들 같은 분, 곧 사람의 모습을 하신 분" (R); "등잔대" for the lampstands

He is Christ, so the honorific is used from the first sight of him. "등잔대" as in Hebrews 9:2 and the Korean Matthew 5:15.

decisions.choice: candelabros
decisions.reason: For the whole book. "Candelabro" is the Portuguese word for the stand of the tabernacle's lamps (m2) and does not imply candles; "castiçal" holds a candle, and "candeeiro" is the oil lamp itself rather than its stand.

source.text: ἡ δὲ κεφαλὴ αὐτοῦ καὶ αἱ τρίχες λευκαὶ ὡς ἔριον λευκόν, ὡς χιών, καὶ οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτοῦ ὡς φλὸξ πυρός, καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὅμοιοι χαλκολιβάνῳ, ὡς ἐν καμίνῳ πεπυρωμένης, καὶ ἡ φωνὴ αὐτοῦ ὡς φωνὴ ὑδάτων πολλῶν, καὶ ἔχων ἐν τῇ δεξιᾷ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ ἀστέρας ἑπτά, καὶ ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ ῥομφαία δίστομος ὀξεῖα ἐκπορευομένη, καὶ ἡ ὄψις αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος φαίνει ἐν τῇ δυνάμει αὐτοῦ.

ko.L: 그분의 머리와 머리털은 흰 양털같이, 눈같이 희고, 그분의 눈은 불꽃 같았다. \v 15 그분의 발은 풀무불에 달군 듯한 빛나는 놋쇠 같았고, 그분의 음성은 많은 물소리 같았다. \v 16 그분은 오른손에 일곱 별을 쥐고 계셨고, 그분의 입에서는 날카로운 양날 칼이 나왔으며, 그분의 얼굴은 해가 힘 있게 비치는 것 같았다.

pt.B: A {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} cabeça e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} cabelos eram brancos como a lã branca, brancos como a neve, e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} olhos eram como chamas de fogo. \v 15 Os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés eram como bronze polido, refinado como numa fornalha, e a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} voz soava como muitas águas. \v 16 Na {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão direita havia sete estrelas, da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} boca saía uma espada afiada de dois gumes, e o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} rosto era luminoso como o sol quando brilha com toda a força.
pt.R: A {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} cabeça e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} cabelos eram brancos como lã ou como neve. Os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} olhos ardiam como fogo. \v 15 Os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés brilhavam como bronze aquecido numa fornalha. A {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} voz era como o barulho de uma grande enchente. \v 16 Ele segurava sete estrelas na {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão direita. Uma espada afiada de dois gumes saía da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} boca. O {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} rosto brilhava como o sol do meio-dia.

decisions.choice: the description draws on Daniel 7 and 10
decisions.reason: White hair like wool belongs in Daniel 7:9 to the Ancient of Days, God himself; here it belongs to the one like a son of man. Eyes like flames of fire, feet like burnished bronze and a voice like the sound of a multitude come from Daniel 10:6, and a voice like the sound of many waters from Ezekiel 43:2, where it is the voice of the God of Israel. The figure has both human form and the marks of God's glory.

decisions.choice: fine bronze: a highly polished metal alloy, glowing as if fired
decisions.reason: χαλκολιβάνῳ is found nowhere before Revelation (also 2:18), and its exact meaning is not known. It is clearly a bright metal, probably a fine alloy of copper, like the polished bronze of Daniel 10:6 and Ezekiel 1:7.

decisions.choice: as if it had been fired in a furnace
decisions.reason: πεπυρωμένης does not agree in form with the word for furnace, and the manuscripts differ here. The sense is clear: the feet glow like metal refined in a furnace. Reviewers should check the variants against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: seven stars: the angels of the seven churches
decisions.reason: Verse 20 explains them. Holding them in his right hand shows that the churches' angels are in his power and care (2:1).

decisions.choice: a sword from the mouth: his word that judges
decisions.reason: ῥομφαία is a long sword. A sword coming from the mouth stands for the power of his word, as in Isaiah 11:4 and 49:2 and Hebrews 4:12. Revelation uses it again for his judgment (2:12, 16; 19:15, 21). The text gives a picture; it is not describing a literal sword.

decisions.choice: Balanced and Readable break the list into sentences
decisions.reason: The Greek runs the whole description as one list, with "and" between each part and no verbs for most of them. Balanced and Readable supply the verbs ("were", "came", "shone") and divide it into sentences.

decisions.choice: sounded like many waters (B); a mighty flood (R)
decisions.reason: φωνὴ means both voice and sound. Balanced keeps "many waters" and makes the voice a sound; Readable uses a picture young readers know.

decisions.choice: bronce bruñido
decisions.reason: The Greek word names a fine, highly polished bronze; "bruñido" says the metal has been polished until it shines, the picture of the meaning decision. Readable says only that the feet shone like heated bronze.

decisions.choice: shaba bora
decisions.reason: The Greek word names a fine, highly polished metal alloy (m2) whose exact makeup is unknown; "shaba bora" (fine bronze) says that without guessing at the alloy.

decisions.choice: "đồng sáng" for fine bronze (also 2:18)
decisions.reason: The word names a highly polished metal alloy glowing as if fired (m2); "đồng sáng" says a bright, burnished bronze. The sword is "hai lưỡi", as in Hebrews 4:12.

decisions.choice: bronze polido
decisions.reason: The exact metal is unknown (m2); "bronze polido" gives the bright, burnished look of Daniel 10:6 in plain Portuguese, where "bronze fino" would be unclear. Also in 2:18.

source.text: Καὶ ὅτε εἶδον αὐτόν, ἔπεσα πρὸς τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ ὡς νεκρός· καὶ ἔθηκεν τὴν δεξιὰν αὐτοῦ ἐπ’ ἐμὲ λέγων· Μὴ φοβοῦ· ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ πρῶτος καὶ ὁ ἔσχατος, καὶ ὁ ζῶν καὶ ἐγενόμην νεκρὸς καὶ ἰδοὺ ζῶν εἰμι εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων καὶ ἔχω τὰς κλεῖς τοῦ θανάτου καὶ τοῦ ᾅδου.

records.literal_gloss: And when I saw him, I fell toward the feet of him as dead; and he placed the right of him on me saying: Not fear; I am the first and the last \v 18 and the living [one], and I became dead and behold living I am into the ages of the ages, and I have the keys of the death and of the Hades.

en.L: And when I saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, I fell at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet as [though] dead. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} placed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right [hand] on me, saying, "Do not be afraid; I am the first and the last \v 18 and the living one, and I became dead, and look, I am alive for the ages of the ages, and I have the keys of death and of Hades.
en.B: At the sight of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} I fell down at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet like a dead man. He laid {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand on me and said, "Do not be afraid. I am the first and the last \v 18 and the one who lives. I was dead, and see, I am alive for all the ages to come, and the keys of death and Hades are {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}.
en.R: When I saw {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, I fell to the ground at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet. I lay there as if I were dead. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand on me and said, "Do not be afraid. I am the first and the last. I was there before all things, and I will be there after all things. \v 18 I am the one who lives. I was dead, but look! Now I am alive forever and ever. I hold the keys to death and to the place of the dead.

fr.L: Et quand je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} vis, je tombai à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds comme mort ; et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} posa {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} [main] droite sur moi, en disant : « N’aie pas peur ; je suis le premier et le dernier, \v 18 et le vivant ; et je suis devenu mort, et voici, je suis vivant pour les siècles des siècles, et j’ai les clés de la mort et de l’Hadès.
fr.B: Quand je {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} vis, je tombai à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds comme un mort. Il posa {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main droite sur moi et dit : « N’aie pas peur. Je suis le premier et le dernier, \v 18 celui qui vit. J’étais mort, et voici, je suis vivant pour tous les siècles à venir, et les clés de la mort et du séjour des morts sont à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Quand je {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ai vu, je suis tombé à terre, à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds. Je restais là, comme mort. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a posé {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} main droite sur moi et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a dit : « N’aie pas peur. Je suis le premier et le dernier. J’existais avant toutes choses, et j’existerai après toutes choses. \v 18 Je suis celui qui vit. J’étais mort, mais regarde ! Maintenant, je suis vivant pour toujours et à jamais. Je tiens les clés de la mort et du séjour des morts.

es.L: Y cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vi, caí a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies como muerto. Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} puso {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} [mano] derecha sobre mí, diciendo: «No temas; yo soy el primero y el último \v 18 y el que vive, y estuve muerto, y mira, estoy vivo por los siglos de los siglos, y tengo las llaves de la muerte y del Hades.
es.B: Al verlo, caí a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies como un muerto. Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} puso {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano derecha sobre mí y dijo: «No tengas miedo. Yo soy el primero y el último \v 18 y el que vive. Estuve muerto, y ya ves: estoy vivo por los siglos de los siglos, y las llaves de la muerte y del Hades son {{deity_pronoun:mías|Mías}}.
es.R: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} vi, caí al suelo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} pies. Quedé tendido como si estuviera muerto. Entonces {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} puso {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} mano derecha sobre mí y me dijo: «No tengas miedo. Yo soy el primero y el último. Yo estaba antes de todas las cosas, y estaré después de todas ellas. \v 18 Yo soy el que vive. Estuve muerto, pero ¡mira! Ahora estoy vivo para siempre. Tengo las llaves de la muerte y del lugar de los muertos.

sw.L: Na nilipomwona, nilianguka miguuni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} kama mfu. Naye akaweka [mkono] {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kulia juu yangu, akisema, "Usiogope; {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni wa kwanza na wa mwisho, \v 18 na aliye hai; nikawa mfu, na tazama, niko hai hata zama za zama, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nina funguo za kifo na za Kuzimu.
sw.B: Nilipomwona, nilianguka miguuni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}} kama mtu aliyekufa. Akaweka mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kulia juu yangu, akasema, "Usiogope. Mimi ni wa kwanza na wa mwisho, \v 18 na ndiye aliye hai. Nilikuwa nimekufa, na tazama, niko hai milele na milele, na funguo za kifo na za Kuzimu ni {{deity_pronoun:zangu|Zangu}}.
sw.R: Nilipomwona, nilianguka chini miguuni {{deity_pronoun:pake|Pake}}. Nililala pale kama mtu aliyekufa. Kisha akaweka mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wa kulia juu yangu, akasema, "Usiogope. Mimi ni wa kwanza na wa mwisho. Nilikuwepo kabla ya vitu vyote, {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitakuwepo baada ya vitu vyote. \v 18 Mimi ndiye ninayeishi. Nilikuwa nimekufa, lakini tazama! Sasa niko hai milele na milele. Nimeshika funguo za kifo na za Kuzimu, mahali pa wafu.

vi.L: Khi thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, tôi ngã xuống dưới chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} như chết. Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đặt tay phải {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên tôi mà nói: "Đừng sợ; {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Đầu Tiên và Cuối Cùng, \v 18 là Đấng Sống, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chết, nhưng kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sống đời đời vô cùng, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} giữ chìa khóa của sự chết và của Ha-đét.
vi.B: Khi thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, tôi ngã xuống dưới chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} như người chết. Ngài đặt tay phải trên tôi và nói: "Đừng sợ. Ta là Đầu Tiên và Cuối Cùng, \v 18 là Đấng Sống. Ta đã chết, nhưng nầy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sống cho đến đời đời vô cùng, và chìa khóa của sự chết và âm phủ thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Khi thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, tôi ngã xuống đất dưới chân {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Tôi nằm đó như thể đã chết. Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đặt tay phải trên tôi và nói: "Đừng sợ. Ta là Đầu Tiên và Cuối Cùng. Ta đã có trước muôn vật, và Ta sẽ còn sau muôn vật. \v 18 Ta là Đấng Sống. Ta đã chết, nhưng hãy xem! Bây giờ Ta sống đời đời. Ta giữ chìa khóa của sự chết và của nơi người chết ở.

ko.L: 내가 그분을 보았을 때, 그분의 발 앞에 엎드러져 죽은 사람같이 되었다. 그분이 오른손을 내 위에 얹으시고 말씀하셨다. "두려워하지 마라. 나는 처음이요 마지막이요, \v 18 살아 있는 이다. 나는 죽었었으나, 보라, 영원무궁하도록 살아 있다. 그리고 내가 죽음과 하데스의 열쇠를 가지고 있다.
ko.B: 그분을 보자 나는 그분의 발 앞에 죽은 사람처럼 쓰러졌다. 그분은 오른손을 내 위에 얹으시고 말씀하셨다. "두려워하지 마라. 나는 처음이요 마지막이며, \v 18 살아 있는 이다. 나는 죽었었지만, 보아라, 영원히 살아 있다. 죽음과 죽은 사람들의 세계의 열쇠가 나에게 있다.
ko.R: 나는 그분을 보고, 그분의 발 앞에 쓰러졌다. 나는 죽은 사람처럼 그대로 누워 있었다. 그러자 그분은 오른손을 내 위에 얹으시고 말씀하셨다. "두려워하지 마라. 나는 처음이요 마지막이다. 나는 모든 것보다 먼저 있었고, 모든 것이 끝난 뒤에도 있을 것이다. \v 18 나는 살아 있는 이다. 나는 죽었었다. 그러나 보아라! 이제 나는 영원히 살아 있다. 나는 죽음과 죽은 사람들이 가는 곳의 열쇠를 가지고 있다.

pt.L: E, quando {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} vi, caí aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés como morto. E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} pôs a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} [mão] direita sobre mim, dizendo: "Não tenha medo; eu sou o primeiro e o último \v 18 e o que vive, e estive morto, e eis que estou vivo pelos séculos dos séculos, e tenho as chaves da morte e do Hades.
pt.B: Quando {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} vi, caí aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés como morto. Ele pôs a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão direita sobre mim e disse: "Não tenha medo. Eu sou o primeiro e o último \v 18 e aquele que vive. Estive morto, e agora, veja, estou vivo para todo o sempre, e as chaves da morte e do mundo dos mortos são {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}}.
pt.R: Quando {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} vi, caí no chão aos {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} pés. Fiquei ali deitado como se estivesse morto. Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} pôs a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mão direita sobre mim e disse: "Não tenha medo. Eu sou o primeiro e o último. Eu já existia antes de todas as coisas e vou existir depois de todas as coisas. \v 18 Eu sou aquele que vive. Eu estive morto, mas veja! Agora estou vivo para todo o sempre. Eu tenho as chaves da morte e do mundo dos mortos.

decisions.choice: the first and the last: God's own title in Isaiah
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 44:6 and 48:12 God says, "I am the first and I am the last", meaning that there is no other God. Here Jesus speaks those words of himself, and in 22:13 he joins them to "the Alpha and the Omega" (compare 1:8).

decisions.choice: the living one, who died and now lives forever
decisions.reason: "The living one" is a name for God (Joshua 3:10; Psalm 42:3). Jesus is the living one, and yet he truly died; ἐγενόμην νεκρὸς, "I became dead", points to a real death at a point in time. His life now is life that will not end.

decisions.choice: the keys of death and Hades: authority over death and the realm of the dead
decisions.reason: To hold the keys is to have authority to open and shut (3:7; Isaiah 22:22). ᾅδου is the Greek name for the place of the dead, the realm the Hebrew Bible calls Sheol. Death and Hades appear together again in 6:8 and 20:13-14. Jesus has authority to release people from death.

decisions.choice: falling as though dead: the response to a vision of God's glory
decisions.reason: Ezekiel (1:28) and Daniel (8:17-18; 10:8-10) fell to the ground before such visions, and in Daniel 10:10-12 a hand touches the prophet and tells him not to be afraid. John's experience follows the same pattern.

decisions.choice: Hades (L, B); the place of the dead (R)
decisions.reason: "Hell" in English means the place of final punishment, which Revelation calls the lake of fire (20:14), and Hades is thrown into it. Literal and Balanced keep the Greek name; Readable says what it is.

decisions.choice: I was there before all things, and I will be there after all things (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title "the first and the last" from its meaning in Isaiah (m1).

decisions.choice: "l'Hadès" (L); "le séjour des morts" (B, R) (for the whole book)
alternatives: "l'Hadès" at Balanced too, as the English Balanced keeps "Hades"
decisions.reason: As the English, French avoids "l'enfer", which names the place of final punishment (the lake of fire, 20:14). The style guide keeps the Greek name at Literal and says "le séjour des morts" at Balanced and Readable, a phrase French readers understand, where the English Balanced keeps "Hades".

decisions.choice: el Hades (L, B); el lugar de los muertos (R)
decisions.reason: Hades is the realm of the dead, not the place of final punishment, so "infierno" would mislead and "sepulcro" is too narrow. Literal and Balanced keep the name, and Readable says what it is, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Kuzimu (L, B); Kuzimu, mahali pa wafu (R)
decisions.reason: "Kuzimu" is the Swahili name for the realm of the dead, used for Hades through the New Testament (Matthew 16:18, Luke 16:23). Readable keeps the name and explains it, as Matthew 16:18 does, where the English Readable replaces it.

decisions.choice: the risen Christ says "Ta" of himself and "nói" when he speaks, through the book
decisions.reason: The style guide gives Jesus "Ta" with its setting span, and the founder settled "nói" for Jesus speaking, as for every speaker. "Đầu Tiên và Cuối Cùng" is God's own title in Isaiah (m1), so Vietnamese capitalises it as a title.

decisions.choice: "Ha-đét" (L); "âm phủ" (B); "nơi người chết ở" (R) for Hades, through the book
decisions.reason: The forms of the Vietnamese Matthew (11:23) for the realm of the dead, which is not the place of punishment.

decisions.choice: "하데스" (L); "죽은 사람들의 세계" (B); "죽은 사람들이 가는 곳" (R), through the book
decisions.reason: Hades is worded as in the Korean Matthew 11:23 and 16:18 and Luke 10:15, so the same word reads alike in the Gospels and here. Christ speaks in 해라체 with "나", as Jesus speaks in the Korean Gospels.

decisions.choice: o Hades (L); o mundo dos mortos (B, R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (6:8; 20:13-14). The style guide's term: Literal keeps the Greek name; Balanced, unlike the English Balanced, says "o mundo dos mortos", since "Hades" is not a word Brazilian readers know outside mythology. "Inferno" would confuse it with the lake of fire (20:14).

source.text: γράψον οὖν ἃ εἶδες καὶ ἃ εἰσὶν καὶ ἃ μέλλει γίνεσθαι μετὰ ταῦτα.

records.literal_gloss: Write therefore what things you saw and what things are and what things are about to happen after these things.

en.L: Write, therefore, the things you saw, and the things that are, and the things that are about to happen after these things.
en.B: So put in writing what you saw, what is, and what will come about after this.
en.R: So write down what you have seen, what is happening now, and what is going to happen after this.

fr.B: Mets donc par écrit ce que tu as vu, ce qui est, et ce qui doit arriver ensuite.
fr.R: Alors écris ce que tu as vu, ce qui se passe maintenant et ce qui va arriver après cela.

es.L: Escribe, pues, las cosas que viste, y las que son, y las que han de suceder después de estas.
es.B: Así que pon por escrito lo que viste, lo que es y lo que va a ocurrir después de esto.
es.R: Así que escribe lo que has visto, lo que está pasando ahora y lo que va a pasar después de esto.

vi.L: Vậy hãy chép những điều con đã thấy, những điều hiện có, và những điều sắp xảy ra sau những điều này.

ko.L: 그러므로 네가 본 것들과 지금 있는 것들과 이 일 후에 일어날 것들을 기록하여라.
ko.B: 그러므로 네가 본 것과 지금 있는 것과 이 뒤에 일어날 일을 기록하여라.
ko.R: 그러므로 네가 본 것과, 지금 일어나고 있는 일과, 앞으로 일어날 일을 적어라.

pt.L: Escreva, portanto, as coisas que você viu, e as que são, e as que estão para acontecer depois destas.
pt.B: Por isso, escreva o que você viu, o que é e o que vai acontecer depois disso.
pt.R: Então escreva o que você viu, o que está acontecendo agora e o que vai acontecer depois disso.

decisions.choice: three things joined by "and": what John saw, what is, and what will happen
alternatives: two things: what John saw, namely both what is and what will happen
decisions.reason: The verse can be read as three parts or as two, with "what you saw" as the heading and the other two as its parts. Some have read it as a plan of the book (chapter 1; chapters 2-3; chapters 4-22), but the visions do not divide so neatly. The question is left open.

decisions.choice: an echo of Daniel 2:28-29 again
decisions.reason: "What is about to happen after these things" recalls Daniel 2:29, as 1:1 does, and is taken up again in 4:1.

source.text: τὸ μυστήριον τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀστέρων οὓς εἶδες ἐπὶ τῆς δεξιᾶς μου, καὶ τὰς ἑπτὰ λυχνίας τὰς χρυσᾶς· οἱ ἑπτὰ ἀστέρες ἄγγελοι τῶν ἑπτὰ ἐκκλησιῶν εἰσίν, καὶ αἱ λυχνίαι αἱ ἑπτὰ ἑπτὰ ἐκκλησίαι εἰσίν.

en.B: As for the mystery of the seven stars you saw in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} right hand and the seven gold lampstands: the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches."

fr.L: [Quant au] mystère des sept étoiles que tu as vues sur {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} [main] droite, et des sept chandeliers d’or : les sept étoiles sont les anges des sept églises, et les sept chandeliers sont sept églises. »
fr.B: Quant au mystère des sept étoiles que tu as vues dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main droite et des sept chandeliers d’or, le voici : les sept étoiles sont les anges des sept églises, et les sept chandeliers sont les sept églises. »
fr.R: Voici le mystère, c’est-à-dire le sens caché, des sept étoiles que tu as vues dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} main droite et des sept chandeliers en or. Les sept étoiles sont les anges des sept églises. Les sept chandeliers sont les sept églises. »

es.L: [En cuanto al] misterio de las siete estrellas que viste en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} [mano] derecha, y de los siete candelabros de oro: las siete estrellas son ángeles de las siete iglesias, y los siete candelabros son siete iglesias».
es.B: En cuanto al misterio de las siete estrellas que viste en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano derecha y de los siete candelabros de oro: las siete estrellas son los ángeles de las siete iglesias, y los siete candelabros son las siete iglesias».
es.R: Este es el misterio, el significado secreto, de las siete estrellas que viste en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} mano derecha y de los siete candelabros de oro. Las siete estrellas son los ángeles de las siete iglesias. Los siete candelabros son las siete iglesias».

sw.L: [Kuhusu] siri ya zile nyota saba ulizoziona katika [mkono] {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wa kulia, na vile vinara saba vya taa vya dhahabu: zile nyota saba ni malaika wa makanisa saba, na vile vinara saba ni makanisa saba."
sw.B: Kuhusu siri ya nyota saba ulizoziona katika mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wa kulia, na ya vinara saba vya taa vya dhahabu: nyota saba ni malaika wa makanisa saba, na vinara saba ni makanisa saba."
sw.R: Hii ndiyo siri, yaani maana iliyofichwa, ya nyota saba ulizoziona katika mkono {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wa kulia, na ya vinara saba vya taa vya dhahabu. Nyota saba ni malaika wa makanisa saba. Vinara saba ni makanisa saba."

vi.L: [Về] sự mầu nhiệm của bảy ngôi sao mà con đã thấy trong tay phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và bảy chân đèn bằng vàng: bảy ngôi sao là thiên sứ của bảy Hội Thánh, và bảy chân đèn là bảy Hội Thánh."
vi.B: Còn về sự mầu nhiệm của bảy ngôi sao con đã thấy trong tay phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và bảy chân đèn bằng vàng: bảy ngôi sao là các thiên sứ của bảy Hội Thánh, và bảy chân đèn là bảy Hội Thánh."
vi.R: Đây là sự mầu nhiệm, tức là ý nghĩa kín giấu, của bảy ngôi sao con đã thấy trong tay phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} và của bảy chân đèn bằng vàng. Bảy ngôi sao là các thiên sứ của bảy Hội Thánh. Bảy chân đèn là bảy Hội Thánh."

ko.L: 네가 내 오른손에서 본 일곱 별과 일곱 금 등잔대의 비밀은 이것이다. 일곱 별은 일곱 교회의 천사들이고, 일곱 등잔대는 일곱 교회이다."
ko.B: 네가 내 오른손에서 본 일곱 별과 일곱 금 등잔대의 비밀은 이러하다. 일곱 별은 일곱 교회의 천사들이고, 일곱 등잔대는 일곱 교회이다."
ko.R: 네가 내 오른손에서 본 일곱 별과 일곱 금 등잔대의 비밀, 곧 그 숨은 뜻은 이것이다. 일곱 별은 일곱 교회의 천사들이다. 일곱 등잔대는 일곱 교회이다."

pt.L: [Quanto ao] mistério das sete estrelas que você viu na {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} [mão] direita e aos sete candelabros de ouro: as sete estrelas são anjos das sete igrejas, e os sete candelabros são sete igrejas."
pt.B: Quanto ao mistério das sete estrelas que você viu na {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão direita e aos sete candelabros de ouro: as sete estrelas são os anjos das sete igrejas, e os sete candelabros são as sete igrejas."
pt.R: Este é o mistério, o significado secreto, das sete estrelas que você viu na {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} mão direita e dos sete candelabros de ouro. As sete estrelas são os anjos das sete igrejas. Os sete candelabros são as sete igrejas."

decisions.choice: mystery: the hidden meaning of a symbol, now explained
decisions.reason: μυστήριον is something hidden that God makes known. Here it is the meaning of what John saw, as in 17:7, where the angel explains "the mystery of the woman".

decisions.choice: a heading: "as for the mystery"
decisions.reason: The opening words stand without a verb, as a heading for the explanation that follows.

decisions.choice: angels: heavenly beings who stand for each church
alternatives: messengers: human leaders or envoys of the churches
decisions.reason: ἄγγελοι means a messenger and is the book's usual word for heavenly angels, as in 1:1. Each message in chapters 2-3 is addressed to the angel of a church, but speaks to the church itself. Some take the angels to be human leaders or messengers, since the word can mean a human messenger (Luke 7:24), but nowhere else in Revelation is it used that way.

decisions.choice: As for (L, B); Here is (R)
decisions.reason: The heading has no verb (m2). Literal and Balanced supply "as for"; Readable makes it a sentence with "here is".

decisions.choice: mystery (L, B); mystery, the secret meaning (R)
decisions.reason: "Mystery" is a key term and stays at every level. Readable adds what it means here.

decisions.choice: misterio (L, B); misterio, el significado secreto (R)
decisions.reason: "Misterio" is the word the Spanish letters use for what God had hidden and now makes known. Readable adds its explanation, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: siri
decisions.reason: "Siri" (a secret) is the hidden meaning of a symbol now made known (m1), the word used for "mystery" in the Swahili letters; "fumbo" would suggest a riddle still to be solved.

decisions.choice: "sự mầu nhiệm"; "thiên sứ" for the angels of the churches
decisions.reason: "Sự mầu nhiệm" is the word of the Vietnamese Colossians (1:26); the meaning decision reads the angels as heavenly beings who stand for each church (m3), so they keep "thiên sứ", the style guide's word for angels, rather than "sứ giả" (messenger), which would choose a human leader.
